notes: Account summary: Fulcrum is a mid-stage fintech that needs sub-100ms p95 for non-streaming LLM responses in its trading-assistant flow; evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and reserved capacity.
Timeline: 2026-02-15 initial intro; 2026-02-22 architecture deep-dive (AE+SE); 2026-03-04 SLA and procurement call (recorded, ff_20260304_8492); 2026-03-09 POC results review.
Key ask: Latency SLOs with contractual measurement approach (p50/p95/p99) + throughput guarantees for reserved GPUs; want 99.9% of traffic within p95 SLA during business hours for production route.

Use-case details: trading-assistant chat = short prompts (~80 tokens) + short completions (~40 tokens) for market signals (high cost of stale latency). Also reranking flow for alerts (bursty, high QPS).
Desired latency targets (customer preference): non-streaming p50 <= 20ms, p95 <= 100ms, p99 <= 250ms; streaming: first-byte p95 <= 120ms, per-chunk p95 <= 40ms.

Measurement alignment requirement: must reconcile client-side timing (end-to-end) vs server-side server-processing-only; Fulcrum insists SLA measured end-to-end from API response visibility in their client (mobile + web).

Redwood proposal: define primary SLA as server-side processing time with a documented client-side delta budget (network/client rendering) and shared instrumentation for cross-checks. Agreed to include both metrics in contract annex.

Streaming vs non-streaming notes: Fulcrum separates routes—streaming for live tick commentary, non-streaming for point-in-time recommendations. Need different SLOs and different measurement hooks (first-byte vs last-token).

Instrumentation plan: enable token-level tracing, request IDs passed through, client SDK timing headers, server-side p50/p95/p99 computed over request processing time (exclude retry/backoff). Synthetic load harness will replicate production RTTs to validate end-to-end.

POC summary (2-week sandbox): workload profile used: 70% chat short-turn, 20% rerank, 10% embedded long-form summarization (control). Avg request size used in tests: prompt 512 tokens (stress case), typical case 120 tokens.

POC results observed: on 4xA100 equivalent reserved pool we saw non-streaming p95 ~120ms (cold starts and batching variability present), p50 ~30ms, p99 ~340ms. Streaming first-byte p95 ~150ms, per-chunk p95 ~60ms.

Inference tuning suggestions: enable prefix KV caching for repeated contexts, reduce batching for critical low-latency routes, tune autoscale burst to keep spare capacity during market opens, consider quantized model variants for deterministic latency.

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask: capacity to sustain 450 reqs/s steady-state with 2x peak factor; Redwood initial sizing estimate = 8xA100 or 4xGH200 depending on model family; will provide cost delta for GH200.

SLA negotiation points (legal): definition of measurement windows, exclusion periods (deployments/maintenance), remediation credits for latency breaches, runbook for incident escalation tied to latency breaches.

Client vs server timing reconciliation: agreed approach = canonical server-side metric for billing/SLA + optional client-side telemetry for debugging; will provide common postmortem artifacts (traces, flame graphs, e2e histograms).

Open technical questions: how to measure streaming per-chunk latency under network jitter; how Redwood handles cross-shard KV cache warming during scale-ups; deterministic test to reproduce p99 spikes.
Commercial notes: Fulcrum prefers an annual reserved commitment but wants a 2-week Dedicated POC to validate latency SLOs before finalizing purchase order. Finance expects decision by 2026-04.
Next steps (technical): produce throughput runbook and target qps-by-route, set up synthetic traffic with client RTT profiles, schedule KMS integration window for test environment.
Next steps (commercial): legal to review SLA annex draft (PR sent), procurement prepping SOW, AE to confirm final ARR cadence and invoicing terms.
Blockers recap: legal SLA language on latency credits, internal budget sign-off for reserved GPUs, network egress testing in Fulcrum VPC, final KMS/HSM verification timeline.
Quotes from calls: 'We will not accept a black-box p95 — need joint measurement and a clear remediation plan' (Fulcrum CTO).
Attachments referenced: fulcrum-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf (pricing sensitivity around GH200 vs A100 sizing), fulcrum-security-faq.pdf (SAML/KMS needs), INF-3124 ticket tracks KMS integration issues.
Sales guidance: position Redwood Optimize to reduce unit cost once SLOs validated; propose staged commit: 6-month reserved with conversion to annual after SLA acceptance.
